newsitem.title: USA: Arnold Schwarzenegger has elective heart surgery.
newsitem.headline: Arnold Schwarzenegger has elective heart surgery.

text.p: Action movie star Arnold Schwarzenegger, a former "Mr Universe" bodybuilder, underwent delicate surgery on Wednesday to correct a congenital heart valve condition, his publicist said.
The 49-year-old Austrian-born actor was expected to make a full recovery from the elective surgery at an undisclosed hospital, the publicist said in a statement.

Schwarzenegger, who is married to television newscaster Maria Shriver, niece of the late President John F. Kennedy, chose to have the surgery to replace an aortic valve, even though it had caused him no health problems, the statement said.
It quoted the actor as saying: "I've never felt sick or had any symptoms at all, but I knew I'd have to take care of this condition sooner or later.
"I said to the doctors: 'Let's do it now while I'm young and healthy,'" the statement quoted him as saying.
The actor, who broke into movies after winning more than 10 major body-building championships, has recently worked with the White House to promote good health and exercise.
After appearing in the 1977 documentary "Pumping Iron," Schwarzenegger went on to star in such Hollywood blockbusters as "Conan the Barbarian" and "The Terminator."
His publicist said he is expected to rest until the end of May, when he will begin promoting his new movie "Batman and Robin" in which he plays the villan, Mr. Freeze.
